title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'Hot Minute', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the old vintage door: an old panelled wooden door with a brass knob, in its own frame, standing alone in the black; warm light under it, then pouring out as it opens (appearing far off, shut, light beneath, gripped, opening, light spilling, open on the party, closing, light under it going out); the reel: nine motif frames: nine small framed images on a black film strip: the high-rise window (01), the tambourine (02/03), the poppy field (13), the stars (05), the candle, the daisy, the magic ride wheel (10), the white temple (11), the burning hourglass (12) (window, tambourine, field, stars, candle, daisy, ride, temple, hourglass); the shut window at the party: a dark, shut window on the party wall, the kind he once went out of (shut, dark); the paper garland: a sagging garland of round paper lanterns across the party ceiling (lit, swaying slowly); gramophone: brass-horn gramophone, a turning record (playing); champagne coupe: a vintage shallow coupe (raised); the rail at the end of the platform: a plain steel rail and cantilevered platform at the end of the Orange Catwalk, stopping in mid-air over the harbour, a lattice strut under it; pale salt stain at 4/10 of the rail's height (clear, haze at the knees, haze over the rail). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
